units.source_text: 自古以来，这个镇子把狗当作不吉利的动物，忌讳它，讨厌它。

en.t: Since ancient times, this town has regarded dogs as unlucky animals, shunning and loathing them.

units.source_text: 有这样一个传说：犬就是“死神的御使”。

en.t: There is a legend that says dogs are the messengers of the god of death.

units.source_text: 一只狗被某家人饲养，这家若死了人，这只饲养的狗就一定会被当作殉葬品，是这个镇上形成的习惯。

en.t: It became the custom in this town that if a family kept a dog and someone in that family died, the dog they had raised would always be treated as a burial offering.

units.source_text: 然而，狗是那样可爱的动物。

en.t: And yet dogs are such lovable animals.

units.source_text: 爱抚狗是人类更古老的习惯。

en.t: Cherishing dogs is an even older habit of humankind.

units.source_text: 这个镇上，也只有饲主家有人死了，才会给狗带来无可奈何的命运。

en.t: Even in this town, only when someone died in the owner's household would an unavoidable fate be brought upon the dog.

units.source_text: 这个镇上深情的人顾忌喂养这种动物，只好忍耐着饲养猫或白兔。

en.t: Tenderhearted people in this town hesitated to keep such an animal, and had no choice but to content themselves with raising cats or white rabbits.

units.source_text: 对自己的鸿运有信心的人，反而饲养两三只，仿佛是夸耀他们家庭幸福的象征，连死神也没有靠近窥视的缝隙。

en.t: Those confident in their own good fortune, by contrast, kept two or three dogs, as if displaying a symbol of their family's happiness, with not even a gap for the god of death to approach and peer in.

units.source_text: 被镇上的人赞赏说“他们养那么多只狗都……”，这家颇感得意。

en.t: When the townspeople praised them, saying, "Even though they keep so many dogs...", the family felt rather proud.
